subject: general
question: In a triangle PQR, length of the side QR is less than twice the length of the side PQ by 3 cm. Length of the side PR exceeds length of the side PQ by 12 cm. If the perimeter of the triangle is 57 cm, then 50% of the length of the smallest side of ΔPQR is equal to:
solution:
**Given:**

In ΔPQR,

QR = (2 × PQ - 3) And PR = PQ + 12

Perimeter of ΔPQR = 57 cm

**Concept used:**

The perimeter of a triangle is the sum of all sides of the triangle

**Calculation:**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c152ae01323aaee700c7052522b78a724bab671d5a7ba1df859d46bfc16365ae.png] 

Let the side PQ be x cm

So,

QR = 2 × PQ - 3 

⇒ QR = (2x - 3) cm

Again 

PR = PQ + 12 

⇒ PR = (x + 12) cm

Now,

(2x - 3) + x + (x + 12) = 57

⇒ 4x + 9 = 57

⇒ 4x = 48

⇒ x = 48/4 = 12 cm

So, PQ = 12 cm

QR = 2 × 12 - 3 = 21 cm

PR = 12 + 12 = 24 cm

So, PQ is the smallest side of the trianngle PQR

So, 50% of PQ = 12 × 50%

⇒ 6 cm

**∴ 50% of the length of the smallest side of ΔPQR is equal to 6 cm.**
